title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2
description:
This is a fight for survival. Xenomorphs swarm in overwhelming numbers. Every room could be your last. 

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 drops up to four players into the boots of Colonial Marines deployed to the most hostile corners of the Aliens universe. This is not a rescue mission – it’s a fight for survival. Xenomorphs stalk the corridors, ambush from the shadows, and swarm in overwhelming numbers. Every room could be your last. Coordinate with your fireteam, leverage each class’s unique abilities, and adapt on the fly as encounters escalate from tense standoffs to all-out war. With deeper squad mechanics, smarter enemies, and a fully customizable Specialist class, AFE2 delivers the definitive co-op Aliens experience. 

4-Player Co-Op Squad Combat
Expanding from three to four players, AFE2 introduces deeper team-based mechanics that reward coordination and strategic class composition. New and improved classes each bring distinct playstyles and tactical abilities to the fight, making every squad combination feel different. 

Xenomorphs That Overwhelm You
The iconic xenomorphs are more ferocious than ever before. AFE2's massive variety of new xenomorphs will force players to stay mobile, maintain situational awareness, and use every tool at their disposal. From stun batons for up close melee action in those most desperate moments, to pyro and electric ammo to whittle down the unrelenting xenomorph front before they overrun you and your squad, the battle can shift from calculated tension to desperate last stand in seconds. 

The Specialist Class -- Play Your Way
Beyond expanded weapon and gear customization, AFE2 introduces the Specialist -- a fully customizable class that lets players mix and match major and minor abilities from every available class. Build a loadout tailored to your exact playstyle and fill whatever role your squad needs. 

Horde Mode -- Survive the Swarm
AFE2 launches with multiple dedicated Horde maps that push squads to their limits. Battle through escalating waves of xenomorphs and other deadly enemies, earning increasingly valuable rewards as you survive deeper into the onslaught. This is where teamwork and skill are tested at their absolute peak.

critic_reviews.quote: Cold Iron Studios has returned to familiar territory to deliver an intense, cooperative experience in which a squad of marines must face off against iconic monsters. While the sequel shares the style of the original, it boasts better level design and is more fun when played as a group of four. The only downside is the numerous minor bugs.
Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 might not be as dramatic of a jump from the original Alien to Aliens, but is nevertheless, a fun and over-the-top action game that fans will enjoy.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 expands on its predecessor with engaging co-op action, focusing on intense xenomorph horde combat rather than horror. The game features a robust build system, encouraging diverse class and weapon use, and a dynamic difficulty that scales with player skill and teamwork. While the core gameplay is fun and the progression system is well-implemented, the high price point, repetitive mission objectives, and performance issues on common hardware are significant drawbacks. Matchmaking can also be frustrating due to specific player requirements.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is the sequel we would have liked to play five years ago: more complete, more flexible in its class system and finally enjoyable even when the bots have to fill the empty seats. Cold Iron fixes a lot, but still relies too heavily on corridors, terminals and repeated swarms to carry a campaign that deserved more variety. The Xenomorphs still do their job, especially with a full squad. Unfortunately, some old habits survived with them.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 improves on its predecessor with better visuals and a handful of welcome refinements. However, many of the same shortcomings remain, while poor optimization and the lack of Korean localization make it difficult to fully recommend.

Your opinion of Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 will largely depend on whether you've played the first game. Newcomers will find a straightforward co-op shooter that captures the spirit of Aliens, albeit with technical issues, repetitive combat, and little reason to continue after the campaign unless they're completionists or simply love blasting xenomorphs. For returning players, the fourth fireteam slot is welcome, but it doesn't make up for the lack of meaningful changes elsewhere. After five years, Fireteam Elite 2 feels more like an expanded version of its predecessor than a true sequel. It's not a bad game, but more substantial gameplay changes, technical fixes, and a sale would make it much easier to recommend.
There’s a fun game in Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 for sure; just don’t expect much in the way of originality.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 offers plenty of replayability through its progression systems, classes, weapons, upgrades, and modifiers, but fails to keep me engaged. While its shallow story, sometimes predictable enemies, limited mission design, poor AI, technical issues, and dull environments hold it back, the game still offers plenty of potential. With the right updates, I might return once the developer has had time to smooth out its rough edges.

Fans of the Alien series are often forced to deal with subpar experiences, and this comes in as one of them. Not withstanding various design decisions brought on by the new team, the quality is simply lacking on many aspects. Combat quickly becomes dry, and at how high of a price this game is, it is not recommended, even to fans of the series.

user_reviews.author: dogmads
user_reviews.quote: I love the Aline's world, and this game took me back to it. I really enjoyed the environments and gameplay overall in this game. I read some people having some bugs with it, but I didn't run into any of them. I played most of it alone and feel like the robots have improved quite a bit from the 1st game. It builds up from the 1st and takes it one or even two levels up. Animation feels better, and having a 4th player makes it even more interesting, being able to fight against bigger xeno's waves.

user_reviews.author: JesperB
user_reviews.quote: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 är ett riktigt underhållande actionspel med intensiv stämning, grymma strider och härlig co-op. Ett måste för fans av Alien-universumet! Loved the first game, love this even more.

user_reviews.author: CeeBeeDee
user_reviews.quote:
15 missions, Tons of weapon and class customization. Ran fine on my machine.

If you like Aliens and AFE this game will do it for ya.

user_reviews.author: ThePixelTourist
user_reviews.quote:
Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is okay, but somehow not as good as its far more polished predecessor: it just looks, sounds, and performs worse. It’s almost baffling, as if the two games were somehow released in the wrong order.

The gameplay is basically unchanged, though, and that might be enough if you’re just looking for more of the same. For everyone else, though, I’d recommend booting up the original Aliens: Fireteam Elite and — if you haven’t done so already — buying the Pathogen expansion instead.

user_reviews.author: MovieWarfare
user_reviews.quote:
The campaign is very boring. Not interesting story-wise, overly repetitive with the same task and missions, the a.i. is not very interesting or smart and the enemy variety isn't that exciting. 

The gameplay itself though is decent fun. Had an enjoyable enough time playing with friends. I do wish there was a bit of variety in weapons between class though. Horde mode is only a lot funner compared to the campaign.

If you have people to play with, this is a decent time
